chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a group from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala ibn Ayub from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Hafs al-A'war from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Ali (peace be upon him) prostrated, he would lower himself as a lean camel lowers itself, meaning its knees. If it is said, 'You have mentioned in the narrations that which includes the permissibility of restricting oneself to a single tasbih in ruku' and sajdah, and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and others have narrated that which refutes you from that.'

key_terms.يَتَخَوَّى: To lower oneself slowly and gently, specifically referring to the act of prostration

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) perform prostration, and what is the debate regarding the number of tasbihs required in ruku' and sujud?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the distinctive physical humility of Imam Ali (AS) during prostration, using the simile of a lean camel lowering its knees to emphasize deep reverence. It serves as a focal point for the scholarly debate on *ikhtisar* (shortening) in prayer, contrasting this report with other traditions from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id that support the permissibility of reciting a single *tasbih* in *ruku'* and *sujood*, thereby illustrating the method of reconciling apparent contradictions in fiqh sources.
